code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for lightheadedness on standing in the heat

text.paragraph: Lightheaded on standing for two days in the heat. [S]

Ms. Hurston, a 67-year-old woman with hypertensive heart disease and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, asked for a same-day visit. For two days, during an early heat wave, she has felt lightheaded each time she stands up, worst in the morning after her pills; yesterday she had to hold the kitchen counter for a few seconds until it passed. She did not fall or lose consciousness. Her house has fans but no air conditioning, she has been working in her garden in the afternoons, and she admits she has drunk less than usual and eaten little at midday. Her home weight is 1 kg below her usual. Her home blood pressure readings have been 104 to 112 systolic. She takes chlorthalidone, amlodipine and spironolactone, all started this spring, and dapagliflozin. She has had no weakness or numbness, no trouble speaking or seeing, no imbalance between episodes, no headache, chest pain, palpitations, vomiting or diarrhea. She knew the BE FAST signs and that this did not match them, but came in because she was worried. [S]

list.item:
Orthostatic hypotension from volume depletion (I95.1). A fall of 24 mmHg on standing, a dry mouth, low home weight and a creatinine of 1.10 mg/dL (from 0.98) fit volume depletion from heat, less fluid and three medicines that remove salt and water. The ECG shows sinus rhythm without arrhythmia, and the neurological examination is normal, with nothing to suggest a stroke or transient ischemic attack. Potassium is 4.4 mmol/L, the first check since spironolactone was added six weeks ago. [S]
Sick-day rules: hold chlorthalidone, spironolactone and dapagliflozin for two days; keep taking amlodipine.
Drink water through the day, about 2 liters, with one glass of an oral rehydration drink; eat regular meals.
Garden in the early morning, not the afternoon; spend the hottest hours in a cooling place such as the library; use fans and cool showers.
Restart all three medicines when the lightheadedness has gone and her home weight is back to usual, and keep weighing daily.
Stand up slowly; sit at once if lightheaded.

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (I50.32). Dry, not congested: no edema and a low jugular venous pressure. [S]
Restart the medicines as above; call if her weight rises more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week after restarting.

Low income (Z59.6). She has no air conditioning and cannot afford to run one. [S]
The community health worker will help her apply for the energy assistance program's cooling help.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); Signs and Symptoms of Stroke (2026); Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (2026)

Follow-up: Nurse telephone call in two days. Eight-week review in two weeks, with a metabolic panel. Call 911 for fainting, chest pain or any BE FAST sign; return the same day if the lightheadedness does not settle. Next scheduled visit 1958-06-01: eight-week review: blood pressure at home and in the clinic, potassium and kidney function, lipids, KCCQ-12 and drug coverage. [S]
